data.title: Meta Creates Nonvoting Stock To Help Zuckerberg Pay California Billionaire Tax
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Meta Platforms Inc. (META) has approved a new class of non-voting stock that could allow CEO Mark Zuckerberg to raise billions of dollars to cover a potential California wealth tax without surrendering his majority voting control.

The Class C common stock, set to take effect in January, will give shareholders one new non-voting share for every Class A or Class B share they own, effectively creating a two-for-one stock split. Meta said the shares could also be used for capital raising, employee compensation and acquisitions, including investments in artificial intelligence.

An SEC filing said Zuckerberg could immediately sell or transfer up to 20 percent of the Class C shares he receives, equivalent to 10 percent of his overall economic stake, including to meet potential liabilities under California Proposition 40.

The proposed measure would impose a one-time 5 percent wealth tax on certain California billionaires. Zuckerberg could reportedly face a tax bill of as much as $11 billion if the measure is approved.

data.title: Allegiant to Buy Six Boeing Planes for $720 Million
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Allegiant Travel is buying six aircraft from Boeing for a total of more than $720 million.

The airline agreed to exercise options under a 2021 deal with the plane manufacturer, providing for the order of six 737-8 aircraft.

The planes are set to be delivered in 2028 and the pricing is subject to discounts and escalations through the slated delivery dates.

There are now 56 firm aircraft under the purchase agreement, 22 of which have been delivered already. There are 74 remaining options under the deal.

data.title: PepsiCo And Taco Bell Extend Partnership Through 2036
data.description:
PURCHASE (dpa-AFX) - PepsiCo (PEP) and Taco Bell have renewed their long-running partnership through 2036, extending a relationship that has produced some of the fast-food chain's best-known menu collaborations.

The agreement means Taco Bell will continue serving PepsiCo beverages and products, including Mountain Dew Baja Blast and Doritos Locos Tacos. The partnership will also cover international markets including Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland and Thailand.

The renewal comes a week after Taco Bell sister chain KFC announced plans to switch to Coca-Cola as its U.S. beverage supplier. PepsiCo's relationship with Taco Bell and parent company Yum Brands dates back decades, before Pepsi spun off its restaurant businesses into a separate publicly traded company in 1997.

Despite KFC's U.S. switch, PepsiCo remains a significant partner for Yum Brands and KFC's international operations.

data.title: General Dynamics Names Amy Johnson President Of GDIT
data.description:
FALLS CHURCH (dpa-AFX) - On Friday, General Dynamics (GD) announced today that Amy Johnson has been appointed as president of GDIT, effective November 3.

Johnson has 27 years of experience at General Dynamics Mission Systems, where she held senior roles in engineering and business leadership across cybersecurity, defense electronics, space and intelligence systems.

Most recently, she served as vice president and general manager for Space, Cyber and Intelligence. She holds bachelor's and master's degrees in computer science and computer systems engineering.

data.title: Gold settles below $4,000 after steepest weekly loss in nearly five months
data.description:
Gold futures fell to three-month lows and silver slumped to its lowest level in nearly a year on ‌Friday, as higher energy prices added to inflation concerns and reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain restrictive monetary policy.

Brent crude oil closed at its highest level in six months as as Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia continued to raise concerns over further disruption to energy supplies and traders bet on renewed fighting in the Middle East after the U.S. midterm election on November 3.

The selloff in tech stocks has also led to margin calls for ​equity traders and investors, causing them to sell gold and silver assets, American Gold Exchange analyst Jim Wyckoff said in a note.

"A rising inflation backdrop along with selling pressure to cover losses in equity or bond market positions is a negative combination for gold in the short-term, even as the Fed is looking assured to keep rates unchanged at next week's FOMC meeting," MUFG's Soojin Kim wrote.

Traders broadly expect the Fed to leave interest rates unchanged at its upcoming October 27-28 meeting, but they see a 78% probability of a hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool.

Two main factors are behind gold's recent swoon, Peter Cardillo of Spartan Capital said in a note - "First, investors are raising cash; second, Russia is selling gold holdings as the war continues to leave its economy in shambles" - but "while the risk of further downside remains, we would selectively buy at these levels."

Front-month Comex gold for October delivery fell 1.3% on Friday to $3,991.10/oz, its lowest settlement value since July 16, and front-month Comex October silver slumped 1.9% to $53.711/oz, its lowest close since November 26, 2025.

For the week, gold and silver fell 4% and 5.7%, respectively.

data.title: Mother of all IPOs! Jio Platforms shatters many existing records - Full list here
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 23 -- The initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms, which attracted strong investor enthusiasm throughout its bidding period, has set multiple new benchmarks in the country's primary market, setting the stage for its stock market debut.

The Street is now betting that Mukesh Ambani's first IPO in 20 years could also make history on listing day by surpassing the debut records of other big-ticket IPOs.

Jio Platforms has become the biggest-ever IPO in the Indian stock market, with an issue size of Rs.30,188 crore, surpassing Hyundai Motor India's Rs.27,858-crore offering, which comprised entirely an offer for sale (OFS).

The issue, which closed on Friday, October 23, attracted bids worth Rs.4.72 lakh crore, making it a major test of investor appetite for large listings at a time when AI-linked stocks are facing increased scrutiny.

The demand also surpassed the comparable interest in LG Electronics India's 2025 IPO. Including bids worth around Rs.2.5 lakh crore for the anchor book, total demand for Jio Platforms' IPO reached approximately Rs.7.4 lakh crore.

The last time an IPO attracted comparable investor interest was Reliance Power's 2008 issue, part of the group led by Anil Ambani.

Jio Platforms' IPO received more than 13.8 million applications, the highest ever in India, a Reliance official told Reuters. In comparison, Chinese memory-chip maker CXMT's $8.6-billion IPO, Asia's biggest listing this year, attracted around 9.4 million accounts.

The IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening on Wednesday, a contrast with many Indian IPOs, where demand typically builds gradually and institutional investors often wait until the final hours to place their bids.

The issue attracted bids worth Rs.67,117 crore on the first day and was subscribed more than three times.

The IPO values Jio Platforms at up to Rs.10.3 lakh crore, potentially making it one of India's largest companies by market capitalisation when its shares begin trading on Wednesday.

Jio Platforms is set to become the 13th publicly listed company under the group. Its listing at the upper end of the price band could take the combined market capitalisation of the Reliance Group to approximately Rs.28.35 lakh crore, potentially surpassing the Tata Group's combined market capitalisation.

The issue comprises an entirely fresh issuance of up to 27 crore equity shares, with no offer-for-sale (OFS) component. This means existing shareholders will not sell their shares through the IPO, and the proceeds from the fresh issue will go to the company.

Retail investors also showed strong interest in the issue, collectively submitting 1.02 crore applications during the three-day bidding period. The retail portion was subscribed 2.76 times, according to exchange data.

Institutional investors showed strong demand for the issue, with the qualified institutional buyer (QIB) portion subscribed 67.15 times and bids exceeding Rs.3.68 lakh crore. The QIB portion was fully subscribed within minutes of the issue opening.

Jio Platforms' IPO anchor book generated unprecedented institutional demand, with bids exceeding Rs.2.5 lakh crore. The anchor portion was oversubscribed more than 30 times its initial size.

data.title: In Florida, Trump vows to deal with Cuba after Iran settled
data.description:
By Bo Erickson, Maria Alejandra Cardona and Steve Holland

US President Donald Trump on Friday used a campaign rally in Florida, where Cuban Americans are a potent voting bloc, to vow to address his concerns about Cuba once the Iran war is settled.

In a 90-minute speech in Fort Myers, Florida, Trump repeated that more military action against Iran may lie ahead as he tries to address the causes of a spike in oil prices that has put Republicans on the defensive ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

With an eye toward the senior Americans who live in Florida, Trump said he planned to spend $250 million to hire at least 5,000 new nurses in elder care facilities all across America.

While the Iran war has no end in sight, Trump talked tough about Cuba, part of a pattern of putting pressure on the communist government there after ousting the leader of Venezuela early this year.

Trump, who won 68% of the Cuban American vote in Florida in the 2024 election, said American naval forces from Iran will stop at Cuba on the way home.

"We'll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They'll raise up their hands, and then we're going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal," he said.

Secretary of State Rubio, a former US senator from Florida, has been handling much of the Cuba portfolio for Trump.

Trump's rally was intended to boost the electoral prospects of Florida Republican Representative Byron Donalds, who is running for governor against Democrat David Jolly.

His speech, the latest in a near-daily blitz of campaign rallies in largely friendly areas, rambled from topic to topic such as the size of his crowds, his White House renovations and his renaming of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America.

Trump has increased pressure on Cuba in his second term. In September, he labeled Cuba a "failed state" at the UN General Assembly and said "freedom will be coming to Cuba," prompting a walkout by the Cuban delegation.

Trump has openly stated that his goal is to fundamentally change Cuba's government. A US-imposed oil blockade has put the country under severe strain as it contends with fuel shortages and blackouts exacerbated by failing infrastructure. UN human rights experts have condemned the oil blockade as a violation of international law.

Trump also escalated his feud with Minnesota Republican Representative Ilhan Omar, a frequent Trump critic, and bashed her home country of Somalia as a "shithouse country."

data.title: Union Minister Piyush Goyal interacts with Indian diaspora in Germany, lauds contribution to 'Karmabhoomi'
data.description:
Berlin, Oct. 23 -- Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal held an insightful interaction with members of the Indian diaspora in Germany, lauding their invaluable contributions to their adopted homeland while calling upon them to actively participate in India's rapid economic growth journey.

In a post on X, the Union Minister expressed immense pride in the achievements of the Indian expatriate community, highlighting their pivotal role as a living bridge in cementing the strategic and economic partnership between India and Germany.

"It is always a pleasure to interact with our Indian diaspora! Had an insightful exchange with members of the Indian diaspora in Germany today," Goyal wrote.

Commending their work ethic and standing in German society, the Minister noted how deeply the Indian community is respected across various professional and cultural sectors abroad.

Meanwhile, addressing members of the Indian community in Berlin, Union Minister Goyal said overseas Indians could serve as a "living bridge" between India and Germany by helping Indian businesses access international markets and establish commercial partnerships.

Union Minister met with Carsten Coesfeld, Member of the Executive Board of Bertelsmann and CEO of Bertelsmann Investments.

"Explored avenues for investment in startups in India and across the media, education & technology sectors," he said.

He also held discussion with Bernd Montag, CEO of Siemens Healthineers AG, on strengthening the company's presence in India and partnering in medical technology and affordable healthcare.

"India's expanding healthcare sector, growing healthcare infrastructure, and focus on accessible care offer immense opportunities to advance MedTech innovation, digitalisation, and AI-driven solutions, bringing quality healthcare closer to every Indian," he said.

Goyal also met Levin Holle, Economic and Financial Policy Advisor to the Federal Chancellor of Germany and G7 & G20 Sherpa, in Berlin.

"Discussed taking forward the India-Germany economic partnership and expanding cooperation on shared global economic priorities and multilateral platforms," he said.

data.title: BP, Louisiana agree to Deepwater Horizon settlement payout, resolve coastal cases
data.description:
BP announced a deal on Friday that provides Louisiana an accelerated, lump-sum $350 million payment to resolve claims over the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill and that also settles long-running coastal damage litigation by local parishes.

• BP agreed in 2015 to pay up to $18.7 billion to the federal government and five states to resolve claims arising out of the oil spill. That money includes $4.9 billion payable over 18 years to settle economic and other claims by the states.

• While Louisiana had been owed $373 million over the next seven years, the state will now receive a single $350 million payment.

• BP said remaining coastal zone lawsuits by Louisiana parishes will be resolved. It did not provide further details.

• "We have now disposed of claims and settled with all but one of the major defendants in these coastal cases," Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry, a Republican, said in a statement distributed by BP.
